title: lcn: r-two56 on a closed food/waste cycle with its core size-limiter weakened (k0 x0.7): shelled worms grow on food, tangle and fragment into shelled rods and cogs, sustaining turnover from full-domain noise
summary: Fork of rf-two56-mu0.01 with a closed nutrient: matter is built from food (Y=2), every loss (negative growth, decay 0.002) becomes waste W that regrows into food at kr=0.02, sum(A)/Y+F+W conserved (asserted every 100 steps); no refill; full-domain noise. The positive control holds: at h0=1 r-two56 cogs form from full-domain noise (17 cogs at t=60) and are static. With the narrow core self-kernel k0 at 0.7 of its weight, shelled worms (cyan core, orange-red shell on both sides) grow at their tips into food wells (black in overview_seed0.png), collide and break into many small shelled rods and cogs (fragmentation_seed0.png, t=196-224); bodies rise from 14 to 49 by t=600 and worms are still present at t=1000; at k0 x0.8 the worms resolve into chains of cogs and die out by t~700, leaving a static cog field (h0_0.8_seed0.png). Food is not yet limiting on average (mean F about 1.0); the shell gate (beta) is implemented but not yet tried, and whether rods/cogs regrow into worms (a real life cycle) is not yet tracked.
